Subject: Agreement edit runbook: renewal term consolidation & capacity scheduling

Marissa — thanks again for the call this morning. Helpful to get alignment on the commercial term and the ramp schedule. Per our notes, Veridian would like:
- A consolidated MSA markup that reflects: 24-month term (with 30- to 60-day early-exit mechanics), the revised indemnity language we discussed, and the data-residency appendix.
- Order form that pins the capacity schedule (Q1: 200k tokens/mo baseline, Q3 add 350k token uplift) and billing proration for mid-quarter increases.
- An explicit addendum for the pilot-to-production ramp guaranteeing capacity hold for the first 90 days after production.

Can you send a single runbook or checklist so our procurement/legal can track the edits and sign path? We want a clean package for legal review by EOD Thursday. Attaching our summary from today.

Thanks — Evan

Attachment: Veridian_request_summary.pdf (summary of call)

Evan — appreciate the clear list. I pulled together a short Agreement Edit Runbook and added owners/timelines below so we have one execution ledger. Please see attached files (tracked-change MSA + order form + billing model).

Runbook (owners / ETA):
1) MSA tracked changes — Priyom (legal) — in review by 11/03 COB. File: Veridian_MSA_marked.docx
2) Order Form version & capacity schedule — Marissa (sales) + Neha (finance) — produce OrderForm_v3.pdf with final numbers by 11/03 10:00 PT
3) Billing proration & tax handling — Neha (finance) — provide Billing_impact_matrix.xlsx and callout for mid-quarter upsell proration by 11/03 14:00 PT
4) Side-letter for ramp guarantee (90d) — Priyom (legal) to draft recommended language for addendum by 11/04
5) Sign path & execution — Marissa to coordinate DocuSign envelope once legal clears. Expected signpath: Veridian legal -> Veridian exec -> Redwood signatory.

Key clarifications we captured from call:
- Term: Veridian prefers 24 months vs Redwood’s standard 12 + auto-renew; client will accept 24 if there is an early-exit taper (30–60 day notice, with pro-rata).
- Indemnity: Veridian asked for limitation carveouts for data residency incidents; Priyom — please call out where we can be flexible without expanding liability exposure.
- Capacity schedule: baseline + explicit uplift windows (we'll hardcode dates on the order form).

Attachments included: Veridian_MSA_marked.docx (track changes), OrderForm_v3.pdf (draft), Billing_impact_matrix.xlsx (initial billing treatment).

Next step: Priyom — can you take the MSA markup and highlight three items that need Exec legal approval vs three items we can resolve administratively? Evan — if your legal wants redlines inline, we'll accept comments back to the doc.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Folks — I went through Veridian_MSA_marked.docx and inserted tracked edits. High-level notes (quick):
1) Term mechanics — fine to agree to 24 months. Need to preserve our cure/termination provisions and clarify the early-exit financial treatment (we should propose a 60-day pro-rata with a step-down on credits rather than full refund).
2) Indemnity/data-residency — proposed carve is acceptable only if we add a narrow definition of "data residency incident" and a cap tied to 6 months of fees for that carveout. I marked this in Section 9.
3) Pilot ramp addendum — recommend an addendum with explicit capacity hold and a failure-to-scale exit clause that reverts to baseline if production SLA targets aren't met; I drafted suggested language under the new Addendum B.
4) Insurance and audit rights — Veridian asked for quarterly audit rights for the first year; push back and offer annual audits + targeted evidence requests for the first 12 months.

I'm attaching a short summary of Exec vs Admin items: Exec items = indemnity carveouts, audit rights expansion, term/early-exit economics. Admin items = order form capacity dates, billing proration mechanics, non-material wording tweaks.

If everyone is aligned, I can finalize the tracked MSA and the side-letter draft tomorrow morning and then hand to Marissa for signpath prep.

Priyom Das
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
